_meta.indication: Topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 12 years of age and older

pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 9 years or older with moderate or severe facial acne vulgaris (IGA score of 3 or 4), 30-75 inflammatory lesions and 30-100 non-inflammatory lesions
pivotal_trials.endpoint: P1: IGA success (IGA score of clear or almost clear and at least a two-point reduction from baseline) at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: IGA success 18.8% (WINLEVI) vs 8.7% (vehicle); difference 10.1% (95% CI 4.1%, 16.0%). Statistically superior to vehicle (p-value ≤ 0.003).

pivotal_trials.population: Subjects 9 years or older with moderate or severe facial acne vulgaris (IGA score of 3 or 4), 30-75 inflammatory lesions and 30-100 non-inflammatory lesions
pivotal_trials.endpoint: P1: IGA success (IGA score of clear or almost clear and at least a two-point reduction from baseline) at Week 12
pivotal_trials.result: IGA success 20.9% (WINLEVI) vs 6.6% (vehicle); difference 14.3% (95% CI 8.9%, 19.7%). Statistically superior to vehicle (p-value ≤ 0.003).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (7 to 12% of patients) are erythema/reddening, pruritus and scaling/dryness; local skin reactions occurred at similar rates in vehicle-treated subjects (e.g., erythema/redness 12.2% WINLEVI vs 15.4% vehicle; scaling/dryness 10.5% vs 10.4%; pruritus 7.7% vs 8.2%). HPA axis suppression was observed (1/20 adults and 2/22 adolescents).
target_moa: Clascoterone is a novel androgen receptor inhibitor that competes with dihydrotestosterone (DHT) for binding to androgen receptors in the skin, limiting or blocking transcription of androgen-responsive genes that modulate sebum production and inflammation; however the exact mechanism in acne is unknown.
modality: Small molecule (steroidal androgen receptor inhibitor); new molecular entity

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was conducted because there were no novel or complex regulatory issues related to efficacy or safety requiring discussion.

summary.text: Standard review of a 505(b)(1) NDA for a new molecular entity; approved based on two adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 trials, with no accelerated approval or special designations and no advisory committee meeting.

Cassiopea SpA submitted new drug application (NDA) 213433 for WINLEVI (clascoterone) cream, 1%, for the topical treatment of acne vulgaris under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway.

The Agency conducted no advisory committee meeting regarding this application because there were no novel or complex regulatory issues related to efficacy or safety that required discussion with subject-matter experts.
